questions.prompt: The bacterial chromosome is typically

options.text: a single circular double-stranded DNA molecule

questions.explanation: Most bacteria have one circular chromosome in the nucleoid. Some, such as Borrelia and Streptomyces, have linear chromosomes.

questions.prompt: DNA replication in bacteria begins at

options.text: a single origin of replication, oriC

questions.explanation: E. coli replicates bidirectionally from oriC. Eukaryotic chromosomes have many origins and have centromeres and telomeres.

questions.prompt: The enzyme that joins Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand is
questions.explanation: Ligase seals the nicks between fragments after DNA polymerase I removes the RNA primers.

questions.prompt: DNA gyrase in bacteria

options.text: relieves supercoiling ahead of the replication fork

questions.explanation: It is a type II topoisomerase and the target of quinolones.

questions.prompt: A DNA strand has the base sequence 5'-ATGC-3'. The complementary strand read 5' to 3' is
questions.explanation: Pairing A with T and G with C gives 3'-TACG-5', which is read 5' to 3' as GCAT.

questions.prompt: During transcription, the enzyme that makes RNA from a DNA template is
questions.explanation: In bacteria one RNA polymerase transcribes all genes, with a sigma factor that recognises the promoter.

questions.prompt: The sigma factor of bacterial RNA polymerase is needed for
questions.explanation: Sigma binds the core enzyme and directs it to the promoter. It is released after initiation.

questions.prompt: The genetic code is described as degenerate because

options.text: more than one codon can code for the same amino acid
a codon codes for more than one amino acid

questions.explanation: There are 64 codons for 20 amino acids, so several codons are synonyms.

questions.prompt: The number of nucleotides in 10 codons is
questions.explanation: Each codon is a triplet, so 10 codons contain 30 nucleotides.

questions.prompt: The start codon of translation in most organisms is
questions.explanation: AUG codes for methionine, which is formylmethionine in bacteria. UAA, UAG and UGA are stop codons.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a stop codon?
questions.explanation: UAA, UAG and UGA end translation. AUG is the start codon, GCU codes for alanine and AAA for lysine.

questions.prompt: In bacteria, translation can begin before transcription is finished because

options.text: there is no nuclear membrane separating the two processes

questions.explanation: The mRNA is read by ribosomes as it is made, a process called coupled transcription and translation.

questions.prompt: Eukaryotic mRNA is different from bacterial mRNA in that it
questions.explanation: Bacterial mRNA is often polycistronic and has a ribosome binding site (Shine-Dalgarno). Eukaryotic mRNA has a cap, a poly-A tail and spliced exons.

questions.prompt: Streptomycin inhibits protein synthesis by binding to the
questions.explanation: Aminoglycosides cause misreading of mRNA and block initiation.

questions.prompt: In the lac operon, the repressor is coded by the
questions.explanation: lacI makes the repressor. lacZ codes for beta-galactosidase, lacY for permease and lacA for transacetylase.

questions.prompt: In the lac operon, high glucose and high lactose gives

options.text: low expression, because of catabolite repression

questions.explanation: Low cyclic AMP means CAP cannot activate transcription, even though the repressor is inactive. Glucose is used first.

questions.prompt: The trp operon is an example of
questions.explanation: When tryptophan is abundant it acts as a corepressor and switches the operon off.

questions.prompt: A mutation that changes one amino acid in a protein is a
questions.explanation: A silent mutation changes the codon but not the amino acid, and a nonsense mutation creates a stop codon.

questions.prompt: A mutagen that inserts between DNA base pairs and causes frameshifts is
questions.explanation: Intercalating agents distort the helix and cause insertions or deletions. UV forms thymine dimers.

questions.prompt: Restriction endonucleases are used in genetic engineering to

options.text: cut DNA at specific recognition sequences

questions.explanation: EcoRI cuts at GAATTC. Fragments are joined by DNA ligase.

questions.prompt: A vector commonly used to carry foreign DNA into Escherichia coli is a
questions.explanation: Plasmids such as pBR322 and pUC carry selectable markers such as ampicillin resistance.

questions.prompt: The polymerase chain reaction needs

options.text: a heat-stable DNA polymerase, primers, nucleotides and a template

questions.explanation: Taq polymerase from Thermus aquaticus survives the denaturation step at about 95 degrees C.

questions.prompt: After 5 cycles of PCR, a single DNA template theoretically gives
questions.explanation: Each cycle doubles the number, so 2 to the power 5 equals 32.

questions.prompt: The steps of one PCR cycle in order are
questions.explanation: Heating separates strands, cooling lets primers bind, and polymerase extends them at about 72 degrees C.

questions.prompt: In gel electrophoresis, DNA fragments move toward the

options.text: positive electrode, because DNA is negatively charged

questions.explanation: Phosphate groups carry negative charge. Smaller fragments move faster through the gel.

questions.prompt: DNA bands on an agarose gel are usually made visible by
questions.explanation: Ethidium bromide intercalates between bases and fluoresces. Safer dyes are also now used.

questions.prompt: Southern blotting is used to detect
questions.explanation: Northern blotting detects RNA and Western blotting detects proteins.

questions.prompt: The transfer of a gene by a bacteriophage that carries any piece of host DNA is called
questions.explanation: In generalised transduction a headful of random host DNA is packaged in error. In specialised transduction only genes near the prophage are carried.

questions.prompt: Hfr cells differ from F plus cells because in Hfr cells

options.text: the F factor is integrated into the chromosome

questions.explanation: Hfr conjugation transfers chromosomal genes starting from the integration site, and the recipient seldom becomes F plus.

questions.prompt: The F factor in F plus cells carries genes for

options.text: sex pilus formation and DNA transfer

questions.explanation: The F plasmid has tra genes for the pilus and transfer machinery.

questions.prompt: Insertion sequences and transposons are

options.text: DNA segments that can move from one site to another

questions.explanation: Transposons often carry antibiotic resistance genes and spread them between plasmids and chromosomes.

questions.prompt: The CRISPR-Cas system in bacteria is a
questions.explanation: Spacers from past phage infections guide Cas nucleases to cut matching DNA. It is now used in genome editing.

questions.prompt: The bacterial genome is enclosed in a nuclear membrane.
questions.explanation: Bacteria lack a nucleus. The DNA is in the nucleoid region of the cytoplasm.

questions.prompt: Plasmids are essential for the survival of a bacterial cell under all conditions.
questions.explanation: Plasmids carry extra, usually non-essential genes such as resistance genes. Cells survive without them in an environment without the selecting drug.

questions.prompt: Translation takes place on ribosomes.
questions.explanation: Ribosomes read mRNA codons and join amino acids brought by tRNA.

questions.prompt: Assertion: Bacterial cells can start translation while mRNA is still being made. Reason: Bacteria lack a nuclear envelope.

options.text: Both the assertion and the reason are true, and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
Both the assertion and the reason are true, but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
The assertion is true but the reason is false
The assertion is false but the reason is true
Both the assertion and the reason are false

questions.explanation: Both are true and the absence of a nuclear envelope allows coupled transcription and translation.

questions.prompt: Assertion: Antibiotic resistance can spread to bacteria of different species. Reason: Plasmids can be transferred by conjugation.

options.text: Both the assertion and the reason are true, and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
Both the assertion and the reason are true, but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
The assertion is true but the reason is false
The assertion is false but the reason is true
Both the assertion and the reason are false

questions.explanation: Both are true. Conjugative plasmids carrying resistance genes may cross species boundaries.

questions.prompt: Assertion: Taq polymerase is used in PCR. Reason: It remains active at the high temperature of the denaturation step.

options.text: Both the assertion and the reason are true, and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
Both the assertion and the reason are true, but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
The assertion is true but the reason is false
The assertion is false but the reason is true
Both the assertion and the reason are false

questions.explanation: Both are true. A normal polymerase would be destroyed at 95 degrees C.

questions.prompt: Assertion: Ultraviolet light is a mutagen. Reason: It forms covalent bonds between adjacent thymines in DNA.

options.text: Both the assertion and the reason are true, and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
Both the assertion and the reason are true, but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
The assertion is true but the reason is false
The assertion is false but the reason is true
Both the assertion and the reason are false

questions.explanation: Both are true. The thymine dimers distort DNA and cause errors in replication if not repaired.
